extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal education funds (K-12 and postsecondary) — Title IX coordinators, school administrators, campus compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance for implementing the §106.45 grievance process under Title IX, covering required contents and timing of written determinations, remedies, hearings/recordings, appeals, record retention, and related procedural protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative report content
rubrics_metrics.description: The investigative report must fairly summarize relevant evidence, but §106.45(b)(5)(vii) does not require the investigative report to describe the investigator's timeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural steps in the investigation will instead appear in the written determination regarding responsibility so both parties understand the investigative process that led to the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written determination: findings of fact and application of Title IX
rubrics_metrics.description: The written determination must include findings of fact supporting the determination and conclusions regarding application of Title IX sexual harassment to those facts (§106.45(b)(7)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement governs how a recipient describes and explains its conclusions regarding Title IX sexual harassment (not how it applies its own code of conduct). The Department revised language to require identification of allegations potentially constituting sexual harassment as defined in §106.30.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written determination: identification of allegations under §106.30
rubrics_metrics.description: The written determination must identify the allegations potentially constituting sexual harassment as defined in §106.30 instead of requiring identification of specific sections of a recipient's code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids implying regulation of a recipient's own code of conduct while still notifying parties how the conduct under adjudication fits within the recipient's unique code of conduct where relevant (e.g., how the recipient's definition of 'consent' was applied).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written determination: disciplinary sanctions and remedies statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The written determination must include any disciplinary sanctions the recipient imposes on the respondent and must state whether remedies will be provided to the complainant (§106.45(b)(7)(ii)(E)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To address privacy concerns, the regulation requires only that the determination state whether remedies will be provided; the nature of remedies need not appear in the written determination and can be discussed separately with the Title IX Coordinator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and nature of remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Remedies may include the same individualized services described in §106.30 as 'supportive measures,' but remedies need not be non-disciplinary or non-punitive and need not avoid burdening the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients have flexibility to offer remedies appropriate to the case; purpose of remedies is to restore or preserve the complainant's equal access to education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator responsible for implementation of remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(7)(iv) states that the Title IX Coordinator is responsible for the effective implementation of remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors the Title IX Coordinator responsibility for supportive measures and ensures a designated official coordinates remedy implementation after a determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordings/transcripts of live hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must make an audiovisual recording, or a transcript, of any live hearing (§106.45(b)(6)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recording/transcript is necessary to preserve the record for appeal and judicial review; parties have equal opportunity to inspect and review it, but the recipient is not required to include it in the written determination or to send copies automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous provision of written determination to both parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision-maker must simultaneously send a copy of the written determination regarding responsibility to both the complainant and respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This promotes transparency and equal treatment and ensures both parties have the same information to exercise appeal rights; privacy concerns are addressed by limiting detailed remedy descriptions in the determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: when a determination becomes final (stay during appeals)
rubrics_metrics.description: A written determination becomes 'final' only after the time period to file an appeal has expired, or, if an appeal is filed, after the appeal decision has been sent to the parties (§106.45(b)(7)(iii)). An appeal by either party 'stays' action on the determination pending resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must offer reasonably prompt time frames for concluding appeals and may use §106.44(c) emergency removal for immediate safety needs; maintaining status quo via supportive measures while an appeal is resolved helps avoid irreversible actions prior to finality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion on when to issue written determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation requires a written determination but does not require it to be issued at the hearing; timing is governed by the recipient's designated, reasonably prompt time frames under §106.45(b)(1)(v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing in the final regulations forces issuance of the determination at the hearing; recipients set reasonably prompt timelines for decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory, equal appeals rights and permitted bases
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer both parties equal appeal rights from determinations regarding responsibility and from dismissal of a formal complaint (§106.45(b)(8)). Appeals must be available on at least three bases: (1) procedural irregularity that affected the outcome; (2) new evidence not reasonably available earlier that could affect the outcome; (3) bias or conflict of interest of the Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decision-maker that affected the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may offer appeals on additional bases but any additional bases must be offered equally to both parties; the revision also removed prior limitations on complainant appeals of sanction severity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals may follow dismissal decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Both parties are expressly permitted to appeal a recipient's dismissal of a formal complaint (or allegations therein), whether dismissal was mandatory or discretionary under §106.45(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal rights include challenges to dismissals as well as to responsibility determinations; recipients must treat parties equally in offering appeal procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable response requirement before sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'equitable response' for a respondent means a grievance process that complies with §106.45 before the imposition of any disciplinary sanctions or other actions that are not supportive measures (§106.44(a) revision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must provide the full procedural protections of §106.45 (hearings, written determinations, appeals, etc.) prior to imposing sanctions beyond supportive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice and uniformity of standard of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may use either a preponderance of the evidence standard or a clear and convincing evidence standard, but must apply the same standard of evidence for complaints against students as for complaints against employees, including faculty (§106.45-related discussion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a recipient chooses preponderance, it must carefully consider whether certain sanctions (e.g., transcript notations) are appropriate under Federal case law; the Department will not dictate which standard to use but requires consistency across complainant/respondent categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcript notations and sender discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department intentionally does not dictate whether recipients should impose transcript notations for respondents found responsible; disciplinary sanction decisions (including transcript notation) rest within recipient discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns about stigma, due process, and long-term harms were noted; respondents may challenge discriminatory sanctions under §106.8(c) or file complaints with OCR. The Department declines to require inter-institutional sharing of Title IX findings (FERPA/privacy issues).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention period
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must retain certain records of a sexual harassment investigation for at least seven years under §106.45(b)(10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This seven-year retention aligns with Department regulations and Clery Act definitions; the requirement applies prospectively. Recipients may destroy records after seven years, but must respect other federal, state, or institutional retention obligations and litigation holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expungement not mandated but permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require expungement of records; recipients may choose to have an expungement process but must still retain required records for at least seven years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients retain discretion to develop expungement policies; they must also avoid discriminatory treatment of records based on sex and comply with other retention laws or obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of investigative/adjudicative functions
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may delegate its obligation to investigate and adjudicate formal complaints to persons or entities not affiliated with the recipient (e.g., regional center model), but Title IX governs the recipient's obligation and the recipient remains responsible for ensuring the grievance process complies with §106.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation does not relieve the recipient of responsibility to issue a written determination and to ensure the process meets regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory scope relative to recipient code of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations govern how a recipient describes and explains conclusions regarding Title IX sexual harassment; they do not purport to regulate a recipient's application of its own code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written determination should transparently disclose how the conduct under investigation 'matches up' against portions of the recipient's code of conduct only insofar as that explains how rules unique to the recipient affect determination or consequences, not to enforce the code itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department deference to recipient disciplinary decisions in OCR review
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.44(b)(2), the Department will not deem a recipient's determination regarding responsibility to be evidence of deliberate indifference to Title IX solely because the Assistant Secretary would have reached a different determination based on independent weighing of the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affords recipients deference in their disciplinary determinations when OCR evaluates compliance, reducing incentives to seek OCR review merely to re-weigh evidence.
